prompt: Put the programs in the order a `docker run` request passes through them.
hint: The client first, the runtime last.

prompt: With a container running, `ps` shows `dockerd`, `containerd`, a shim and `sleep`, but no `runc`. Why?
hint: What is runc's job, and when is it done?

choices.text: It exits once the container is created
choices.why: Right: it sets up namespaces and cgroups, starts the process, and leaves the shim in charge.

choices.text: runc crashed after starting the container
choices.why: Nothing failed; exiting is what runc does.

choices.text: runc runs inside the container, where the host cannot list it
choices.why: The host lists every process, including the container's `sleep`.

choices.text: Docker 29 replaced runc with containerd
choices.why: `docker version` still lists runc 1.5.1.

prompt: What does keeping one shim per container make possible?
hint: What happens to containers when `dockerd` is upgraded?

choices.text: Running Windows containers on a Linux host, with no VM in between
choices.why: No shim can supply a different kernel.

choices.text: Upgrading the daemons without killing running containers
choices.why: Right: `dockerd` and `containerd` can be restarted or upgraded while the shim holds the container's input, output and exit code.

choices.text: Starting containers without an image
choices.why: Every container still needs a root filesystem.

choices.text: Sharing one writable layer between many containers started from one image
choices.why: Each container still has its own; the shim has nothing to do with layers.

prompt: `curl --unix-socket /var/run/docker.sock http://localhost/containers/json` returned the running containers. What does that show about the `docker` command?

choices.text: It reads containers straight from `/var/lib/docker`
choices.why: It never reads that directory; it asks the daemon.

choices.text: It needs `curl` installed to work
choices.why: It speaks the API itself; `curl` was only a second client.

choices.text: It is a client of an HTTP API open to any program
choices.why: Right. `docker ps` sends exactly this request.

choices.text: It talks to Docker Hub to list containers
choices.why: Containers are local; the request went to the local daemon.

prompt: Match each program to its job.

pairs.right: Holds images, networks, volumes and the record of containers
Unpacks images into snapshots and starts and stops containers
Stays beside one container, holding its output and exit code
Creates the namespaces and cgroups and starts the process

right_distractors: Pulls images on behalf of Docker Hub's servers

prompt: Why does the lesson install Docker Engine from Docker's own repository rather than the distribution's?

choices.text: The distribution's packages are illegal to use in companies
choices.why: Nothing about them is illegal; they are older and packaged differently.

choices.text: It is the only way to get a Docker Hub account
choices.why: Accounts have nothing to do with how the engine is installed.

choices.text: Ubuntu forbids third-party repositories
choices.why: `apt` supports them; the key in `signed-by` is how it trusts one.

choices.text: It has the current engine and the Compose and Buildx plugins
choices.why: Right, built for each supported distribution.

prompt: In the repository line, what does `signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc` make `apt` do?

choices.text: Accept only packages carrying Docker's signature
choices.why: Right. The key is how apt knows the packages came from Docker.

choices.text: Encrypt the downloaded packages on disk
choices.why: Signing proves origin; nothing here encrypts.

choices.text: Download faster from a mirror
choices.why: The key says nothing about speed or mirrors.

choices.text: Log in to Docker Hub with Ana's account
choices.why: The key belongs to Docker's package repository, not to an account.

prompt: `sudo -u bruno docker ps` printed "permission denied while trying to connect to the docker API". What is missing?

choices.text: A Docker Hub login for Bruno
choices.why: Listing local containers needs no registry account.

choices.text: Bruno's membership of the `docker` group
choices.why: Right. The socket is `rw` for root and the `docker` group only.

choices.text: A second daemon for Bruno's user
choices.why: One daemon serves every allowed user.

choices.text: The `docker-ce-cli` package in Bruno's home directory
choices.why: The command ran; the socket refused him.

prompt: Ana could not list `/srv/payroll` but read `salaries.csv` through `docker run -v /srv/payroll:/p`. What is the right conclusion?

choices.text: Docker has a bug in how it checks permissions on mounts
choices.why: It is behaving as designed; the daemon runs as root and does what it is asked.

choices.text: The file's permissions were set wrongly by the lab
choices.why: They are `600`, root only, as intended; Ana really cannot read it as herself.

choices.text: Membership of the `docker` group is equivalent to root on that machine
choices.why: Right. Grant it only to people you would give root.

choices.text: Bind mounts are read-only, so nothing was really exposed
choices.why: She printed the contents; mounts are writable unless `:ro` is asked for.

choices.text: Containers can no longer run as root inside them, so images that expect root refuse to start
choices.why: Inside, a process can still be root; outside, that root is only the user.

choices.text: Only the `docker` group is removed
choices.why: The change is to the daemon's own privileges.

choices.text: Images are pulled without a registry
choices.why: Pulling works the same; the daemon's user is what changes.

choices.text: The daemon itself runs as an ordinary user, so a container's root is only that user
choices.why: Right, at the cost of some limits Docker documents.

prompt: The lab's `daemon.json` sets `registry-mirrors` to `https://mirror.gcr.io`. Ana pulls `alpine:3.22`. What changes compared with a pull straight from Docker Hub?
hint: Names, tags, digests, and the server.

choices.text: Only the server that sends the bytes
choices.why: Right. The name, tag and digest are Docker Hub's.

choices.text: The image gets a different digest
choices.why: The digests stay Docker Hub's; the bytes are the same.

choices.text: The image is renamed `mirror.gcr.io/alpine`
choices.why: It is still `alpine:3.22`, as `docker image ls` showed in lesson 1.

choices.text: Ana has to log in to Google
choices.why: The mirror is public; no login is needed.

prompt: Bruno edits `/etc/docker/daemon.json`, leaves a trailing comma, and restarts Docker. What happens?
hint: When does the daemon read the file?

choices.text: The daemon ignores the bad line and starts
choices.why: It reads the whole file at start and refuses a malformed one.

choices.text: The daemon does not start
choices.why: Right. Checking the file with `jq .` before restarting avoids it.

choices.text: Docker rewrites the file without the comma
choices.why: Nothing rewrites it; the file is the administrator's.

choices.text: Only new containers are affected
choices.why: Without a daemon, no container can be managed at all.

prompt: `Logging Driver: json-file`. Where does `docker logs` read a container's output from?

choices.text: Docker Hub's logging service
choices.why: Nothing about logs leaves the machine with this driver.

choices.text: The container's writable layer, under `/var/log`
choices.why: The engine captures the output; it does not read files inside the container.

choices.text: A file of JSON lines on the same machine
choices.why: Right, and by default it grows without a limit; lesson 18 sets one.

choices.text: The terminal that started the container, which keeps a copy in memory
choices.why: A terminal keeps nothing; the engine stored the output.

prompt: `docker info` reports where the engine keeps its images, containers and volumes on disk: the `Docker Root Dir`, which on the lab is ___.
Match each machine to what the lesson says to install on it.

pairs.right: Docker Desktop, or an alternative that runs a Linux VM

pairs.left: A Linux CI runner building images

right_distractors: Docker Desktop's Linux VM on a Linux server

prompt: `/var/lib/docker` has grown to 40 GB on a build server. What should Bruno avoid doing?
hint: Who keeps the records of what is in there?

choices.text: Asking Docker what is taking the space
choices.why: That is the safe first step, and lesson 22 shows it.

choices.text: Removing images nobody uses through `docker`
choices.why: Going through the daemon keeps its records right.

choices.text: Checking it with `sudo du -sh /var/lib/docker`
choices.why: Reading the size changes nothing.

choices.text: Deleting files inside it by hand
choices.why: Right. The daemon's records and the files would disagree; lesson 22 reclaims space safely.

prompt: On an ordinary Ubuntu server, the Docker daemon has stopped. Which command starts it again?

choices.text: `sudo systemctl start docker`
choices.why: Right. The lab cannot run it, because it does not boot with systemd.

choices.text: `docker start`
choices.why: That starts a stopped container, and it needs a running daemon to ask.

choices.text: `docker run dockerd`
choices.why: No container can start without a daemon to start it.

choices.text: `sudo apt-get install docker-ce`
choices.why: It is already installed; it only needs starting.
